editorial.headline: Real Estate Appraisal: Open Nationally, Viable in Bali at Higher Risk
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 68291 covers real-estate valuation services, open to foreign investment nationally and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
Real-estate appraisal is a specialised service activity centred on determining the value of real property. KBLI 68291 covers services that appraise the value of real-estate property: the commercial focus is valuation itself, rather than a broader claim over the property market. It is a precise category for businesses whose work concerns the assessed worth of real estate.

The activity is open across the full business-scale range stated in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That breadth matters because the code is not confined to one narrow size of enterprise. A business may register this activity at any of those listed scales, while retaining the same essential focus on real-estate valuation services.

Nationally, the PMA position is straightforward. The activity is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, foreign investment is open at the national level and the record does not impose a lower national foreign-equity cap. The stated basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali does not reverse that national opening. The province’s permanent, island-wide PMA moratorium applies to Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities; this activity is not blocked by that rule. At the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, which places it outside the moratorium’s blocked risk bands. For a foreign investor considering this specific appraisal activity in Bali today, the record’s conclusion is clear: PMA registration is not blocked there.
